_doc: Meeting script templates for crewmates. Keys are situations detected by the engine. Placeholders: {P} target player, {R} room, {T} time (m:ss), {W} witness, {V} victim, {TASK} task name, {N} number. Each entry: question templates (ask), statement templates (say), what to watch for. Keep lines ≤ 90 chars.
principles: Give your own location + companion FIRST. It pre-empts accusations and models the behaviour you want.
Lead with hard clears. A confirmed-crew list is the most valuable thing you can say.
Ask questions whose answers can be checked against what someone else saw.
Make people commit to a story early; contradictions only exist once stories are on record.
Vote skip when nobody has evidence. A wrong eject is worth more than a kill to the impostors.
Watch who agrees without adding info. Bandwagons hide impostors.
Count. Alive crew vs impostors decides whether a skip is safe.

say: I was in {R} with {W} the whole round.
I saw {P} do {TASK} in {R} — visual, {P} is clear.
ask: Where was everyone when the body was found? Start with people near {R}.
watch: Anyone who answers with a question instead of a location.

ask: {P}, you reported in {R} — who did you see on the way there and why were you going there?
{P}, what task takes you to {R}? I don't have one there.
say: {P} reported alone in {R}. Nobody saw them arrive. Not an accusation yet — a question.
watch: If {P} names a task that isn't in {R} on this map.
If {P} names a companion who then denies it.

ask: {R} is a dead end. Who was last seen going in or coming out? I saw {P} leaving around {T}.
say: Body in {R} — only one way in. Whoever was last through that doorway needs a reason.
watch: Vent networks touching {R}: anyone who 'appeared' nearby without passing the door.

ask: {P}, you were with {V} in {R} at ~{T}. Where did you split and where did you go?
say: Last person I saw with {V} was {P}, in {R}, around {T}.
watch: Whether {P} offers the split location unprompted or deflects.

ask: {P}, you said you did {TASK} in {R}. That's a common task — everyone has it. Who else has it?
say: I don't have {TASK}. Common tasks are the same for all crew. Someone's list is wrong.
watch: Anyone who suddenly 'also has it' with no location.
This is near-proof if the lobby's common tasks are known.

say: {TASK} isn't in {R} on this map. {P}, which panel did you use?
watch: Specificity. Crew can name the panel; impostors go vague.

ask: {P}, you claim {TASK} — that's visual. Who saw the animation?
say: Visuals are on. If nobody saw {P}'s {TASK}, that claim is worthless until someone does.
watch: If {P} downgrades to a non-visual task after being asked.

ask: When lights went down, who went to Electrical and who didn't? I saw {P} arrive late from {R}.
say: Kill happened during lights. Impostor vision isn't reduced — whoever was 'lost' is the question.
watch: Anyone who claims they were 'on the way' but arrived from the wrong direction.

ask: {P}, reactor was called and you didn't show at either panel. Where were you?
say: {W} and I fixed {TASK} together — {W} is clear for that window.
watch: Who benefits from a split: the impostor usually ends up on the smaller side.

say: {P} said {R} at {T}. {W} saw {P} in {R2} at the same time. One of those is wrong.
That's not what {P} said last meeting.
ask: {P}, {W} says you were in {R2}, not {R}. Which is it?
watch: Whether {P} attacks {W}'s credibility instead of answering.

ask: {P}, what did you actually see? 'Sus' isn't a location.
say: {P} is pushing {P2} with no sighting. Where were you, {P}?
watch: Impostors often accuse first to look proactive.

say: Hard clears only now: {W} is confirmed crew (visual/kill-window). Everyone else is on the table.
Count: {N} impostors left. We cannot skip.
ask: {P}, {P2} — each of you, where were you for the last kill? Precise room and time.
watch: The impostor will try to make it a vibe vote. Keep it to kill windows.

say: Nobody has evidence. Skip and stack — move in groups of two next round.
ask: Can everyone at least say their room and who they were with? Record it for next meeting.
watch: Who resists committing to a location.

say: {P} hard-defended {P2} who just got confirmed impostor. That's a pair tell.
ask: {P}, why were you sure {P2} was clear?
watch: Any two players who never vote each other across meetings.

say: Kill in a stack: {P}, {P2}, {P3} were all there. Impostor is in that group. Who was closest to {V}?
ask: Each of you three: who did you see with the body before the report?
watch: The one who claims they 'didn't notice' the kill.
